requirements.invariant: OperationID alone is one global idempotency identity. It is not namespaced by Account, Principal, device, command family, payload type, or fingerprint; every present local evidence row for that ID reserves it while present.

One centralized ID-scoped inspection inventories local operation, synchronized result, every exact ps_crud command entry produced by a known insert-only command view, any ps_crud entry for a forbidden local mutation of the synchronized operation-result relation, pending Client/Project/allocation projection, archive overlay, and local-only assignment command. Pinned PowerSync 0.5.3 does not persist a second backing command row for an insert-only write, so no phantom representation is required. A queued operation-result mutation is malformed reservation evidence, not a command family. Ambiguous pending Client evidence reserves but never identifies a family by itself. A future relation/provider must be registered once in this inventory before its implementation can advance.

No evidence permits a new claim. A typed same-family owner may proceed only to provider state-aware replay validation. A canonical typed applied or rejected creation row is a valid sole survivor after its ps_crud command and reconciled/rejected pending projection drain; any pending graph still present must validate exactly, and this slice authorizes no new cleanup. Queued/applying or untyped/malformed operation-only evidence remains incomplete and fails closed. A complete different-family owner or changed fingerprint is payloadMismatch even when fingerprints are deliberately equal across families. Other orphaned, malformed, ambiguous, multi-family, result-only, result-mutation-queue-only, pending-only, overlay-only, or command-only evidence fails closed without repair, deletion, or rebinding.

Guard inspection, replay classification, normal ownership insert, and all family-specific writes occur in one provider writeTransaction. Same-family concurrency converges; different-family same-ID concurrency commits exactly one graph and returns one deterministic mismatch/refusal with no partial second family.

All five current local accepting providers use the same guard before replay or mutation that reaches SQL. Client and Project creation begin persisting explicit create_client/create_project family and canonical envelope evidence and validate owner Account, Principal, contract, fingerprint, subject, state, and family on replay. Existing archive-family ID-prefix validation remains before SQL; Project-archive and Client-archive public IDs are disjoint, while direct synthetic guard proof still classifies corrupt stored evidence for that pair in both directions. Existing family-specific command, precondition, projection, upload, and result semantics otherwise remain unchanged.

Pre-foundation untyped evidence may derive a family only from one unambiguous surviving graph; otherwise it remains reserved and fails closed. There is no shipped target database to migrate. Valid ownership and malformed reservation behavior survive encrypted restart, while synthetic pre-foundation databases may be discarded without repair or production migration.

The existing owning Account runtime or constructor-bound store scope checks refuse Account/Principal mismatch before SQL access. Client and Project creation remain runtime-bound database-only stores; this slice does not add constructor scope to them. Stable OperationContractFailure.payloadMismatch may echo only the caller-supplied OperationID already present in the submitted command. No error exposes a stored foreign identifier, stored payload field, foreign scope, SQL, path, credential, provider message, or cross-tenant ownership detail. CancellationError remains control flow through every accepting provider; raw inspection failures map through each provider's bounded local-acceptance error without mutation. Default-no-op internal checkpoints may be added only to inject deterministic inventory/post-inspection/family-write/pre-/post-commit failures for proof and are not a production behavior surface.

This guard adds no second registry table, synchronized row, ps_crud entry, upload shape, projection, cleanup/retention policy, server schema/handler/RLS/Sync behavior, app/MCP feature, hosted resource, source-backend change, migration execution, production access, release, or cutover authority. Clearing remains DRAFT until this prerequisite is verified, then registers its one new family/relation centrally.

verification.expected: The centralized inventory names exactly five current command families, all current operation-bearing relations, all four exact ps_crud command entry types produced by the insert-only command views, and the forbidden operation-result relation ps_crud type; OperationID alone is the key and ambiguous pending Client evidence never invents a family. Against the frozen PowerSync core, inserting each command view produces exactly one matching ps_crud entry and zero query-visible/backing command row.

Direct synthetic guard evidence covers every ordered pair of the five families and refuses reuse in both directions. Public store submission covers every pair whose ID formats overlap; the disjoint Project-archive/Client-archive pair proves existing pre-database invalid-identity refusal instead of claiming guard mediation. Exact same-family replay succeeds, changed replay fails, and deliberately equal fingerprint across different command types still mismatches.

Concurrent same-ID claims from independent store instances cover every unordered distinct-family pair whose public ID formats overlap and every family raced against itself. The disjoint Project-archive/Client-archive pair proves pre-database invalid-identity refusal plus direct synthetic guard classification rather than an impossible public race. A feasible distinct-family race commits exactly one complete graph and the other refuses deterministically. An equal-payload same-family race converges on one graph and matching receipts; a changed-payload same-family race produces one winner and one payload mismatch. No case creates a second ps_crud entry, projection, pending count, graph, or receipt.

Each operation-bearing relation, each exact ps_crud command type produced by an insert-only view, and the forbidden operation-result relation ps_crud type, isolated as an orphan against every destination family, reserves the ID. Result-only, result-mutation-queue-only, pending-only, overlay-only, ps_crud-command-only, ambiguous pending-Client, multiple-family, malformed JSON/type, foreign-scope, and untyped/malformed/nonterminal operation-only graphs fail without mutation or stored/foreign disclosure. payloadMismatch may contain only the caller-supplied OperationID. A typed canonical terminal create operation is explicitly excluded from the orphan class and is covered by positive replay proof.

Owner family, Account, Principal, contract, fingerprint, subject, canonical envelope, state, result, and required auxiliary tampering fail closed. New create rows carry explicit family/envelope; untyped legacy evidence derives only from one unambiguous graph and otherwise remains reserved. For both create families, applied replay stays exact after transaction.complete drains ps_crud with the pending graph intact and again after authoritative reconciliation removes it; rejected replay stays exact after ps_crud and required pending rows drain. No new pending cleanup is introduced, and typed terminal-row or any still-present pending-graph tampering fails closed.

Default-no-op deterministic inventory-read, post-inspection, family-write, pre-commit, and post-commit failure/cancellation checkpoints in all five stores prove one transaction, rollback before commit, durable acceptance after commit, CancellationError passthrough before generic mapping, and bounded raw-error/guard-error translation.
Valid owner/replay and every malformed reservation class remain byte-equivalent in behavior across repeated encrypted close/reopen; no bootstrap backfill, repair, or deletion occurs.
